files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Owner: C. Reyes. Complete sequentially; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and underlying contracts. Check the GL first to prevent duplication. If it has not been recorded, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to ensure it has not already been posted.
5. Verify the expense coding on June vendor bills by comparing the bill documents with the GL. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after all entries and reclasses from steps 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Ember Signal Inc. began in 2019, when a product engineer and a customer-operations lead grew tired of watching small software teams piece together alerts, status updates, and customer communications across a crowded collection of tools. They built a lightweight shared console that turned noisy system events into clear, assignable signals. Early users liked that it was practical rather than flashy, and the product gradually developed into a focused SaaS platform for monitoring workflows, incident coordination, and operational reporting.

Today, Ember Signal Inc. sells hosted software to growing businesses whose teams need a common view of service health and follow-up work. Customers use the platform to route alerts, document responses, spot recurring issues, and keep internal stakeholders informed without adding another complicated enterprise system.

The team has a distinctly hands-on flavor. Engineers regularly sit in on support reviews, customer-success staff contribute to product planning, and sales conversations tend to begin with workflow questions rather than polished demos. Internal writing is direct, with a preference for checklists, short decisions, and named owners.

The company is currently refining its core product, improving onboarding, and building a more repeatable approach to partnerships and demand generation. It remains an ordinary going concern, balancing steady customer service with the operational discipline expected of a maturing SaaS business.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Ember Signal Inc. should sound like the calm operator in a noisy category: practical, credible, and close to the work. The H2 program will tighten the brand story around clearer signals, faster ownership, and less operational clutter.

## Priorities

- Refresh core messaging and visual guidance without forcing a wholesale rebrand.
- Publish customer-led material that shows real monitoring and incident workflows.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, alternating between operator roundtables and product walkthroughs.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with complementary SaaS providers and specialist consultancies.
- Give sales a smaller, cleaner set of proof points, email sequences, and follow-up assets.

## Quarter plan

### Q3

Finalize positioning, update high-traffic pages, interview customers, and prepare the first webinar series. Select partner candidates based on audience fit and willingness to share execution.

### Q4

Launch the co-marketing pilot, expand the strongest webinar themes into written content, and review lead quality with sales. Retire channels that create activity without useful conversations.

## Measurement

Track qualified engagement, webinar attendance quality, partner-sourced conversations, content-assisted opportunities, and sales feedback. The team will review results after each campaign and document what to repeat, revise, or stop.

# Notes from your chatty predecessor

C. Reyes — a few things worth knowing before you get too deep into the close:

- The bank's own service fees and charges usually appear near the end of the statement. We have historically picked those up and booked them during close, so do not assume the ledger already has them.
- Please give the June vendor-bill coding a real look. A couple of expenses may be sitting in the wrong accounts, and the supporting documents in `bills/` are authoritative if the GL description tells a different story.
- The Q2 budget was fixed in early April. As a result, the one-off items that arrived in June were never planned, and they are the reason some of the larger variances will stand out.
- One payroll timing wrinkle this month: the June 16-30 payroll run does not pay until the first days of July. The payroll register has the detail, but do not miss the accrual.
